Incorporating the Beige Book with the Dec 14, 2022 FOMC action, SLOOS, and the FSR tilts the outlook more negative than a policy-only read:

- Beige Book signals: Most districts reported flat-to-slower activity, with housing and CRE weakening (e.g., Boston, New York). Banks noted softer loan demand and tighter credit standards, with early signs of rising delinquencies. Many contacts expected an economic downturn in 2023.
- Offsets: Services spending (e.g., restaurants) held up in some areas, labor markets remained tight though easing at the margin, and price increases showed some moderation from peak levels.
- Net: Beige Book corroborates SLOOS and FSR—tightening credit supply and weakening demand are transmitting policy more forcefully, raising downside growth risks despite some service-sector resilience.
